source_meta._title: Wind Burst book available from villager trading

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 24w13a in a fresh single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled. Enable the built-in Update 1.21 experiment so that the mace and Wind Burst content are present; leave the separate Villager Trade Rebalance experiment disabled to avoid changing the ordinary librarian trade pool.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected snapshot 24w13a. Do not use fix version 1.20.5 Pre-Release 1.
Use a disposable test world rather than an important save because this is an old snapshot.

At world creation, enable the Update 1.21 experimental feature set. Java experimental features are exposed through per-world feature toggles. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/ja-jp/article/testing-new-minecraft-features/feature-toggles-java-edition?utm_source=openai))
Creative mode and cheats are practical setup choices because the report does not specify a game mode and the test requires repeatedly obtaining blocks and variable trade inputs.
Use one adult, unemployed villager. Do not use a baby villager, a green-clothed nitwit, or a villager whose trades have already been used.
Perform the test in a clear area without other villagers, lecterns, or workstation blocks that could interfere with workstation assignment.
The Wind Burst offer is randomly generated in this affected version. The report provides no seed or guaranteed reroll count, so an unknown number of lectern replacements may be required.
Accept any displayed Wind Burst enchantment level and price; the report does not require a particular level or emerald cost.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation using snapshot 24w13a, launch it, and verify that the main menu displays 24w13a.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft: Java Edition main menu is open and identifies the running version as 24w13a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and ensure commands/cheats are allowed. No particular seed is required because the report supplies none.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative mode and commands are available for the new world.

steps.action: Before creating the world, open the world-creation Experiments menu, enable the experiment named Update 1.21, confirm the warning if one appears, and leave Villager Trade Rebalance disabled.
steps.success_cue: Update 1.21 is enabled while Villager Trade Rebalance remains disabled on the world-creation screen.

steps.action: Create the world and wait without interacting until terrain has rendered and normal movement responds immediately.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the new world, nearby chunks are rendered, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the time command with the leading slash, and press Enter. Keeping the test in daytime makes workstation assignment easier to observe.
steps.success_cue: The world changes to daytime and the command reports successful execution.

steps.action: Press T again, enter the daylight-cycle command with the leading slash, and press Enter so the test does not unexpectedly advance out of villager working time during repeated rerolls.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that doDaylightCycle is now false and daylight remains fixed.

steps.action: Move to clear level ground away from any visible village, other villager, lectern, or workstation. Press E to open the Creative inventory, use the Search Items tab, and place a Villager Spawn Egg, a Lectern, and a stack of any solid building block into the hotbar.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a Villager Spawn Egg, a Lectern, and solid blocks, and the selected test area has no competing workstation setup.

steps.action: Using the solid blocks, construct a small roofless containment pen with at least two floor spaces inside and walls two blocks high. Leave enough room for one villager and one lectern. The pen only prevents the villager from wandering during rerolls.
steps.success_cue: A roofless pen with two-block-high walls and space for a villager beside a lectern is complete.

steps.action: Select the Villager Spawn Egg in the hotbar and right-click the floor inside the pen once. Inspect the spawned villager. If it is a baby, or if it wears the solid green nitwit outfit, remove it in Creative mode and spawn another. Use an adult villager that initially has no workstation profession.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one adult, non-nitwit villager is contained in the pen and has not previously been traded with.

steps.action: Select the Lectern in the hotbar and right-click the floor space immediately beside the villager to place it.
steps.success_cue: One lectern is placed next to the contained villager, with no other lectern or workstation competing for that villager.

steps.action: Wait until the villager claims the lectern. Watch for profession-change particles and the librarian appearance; do not continue while the villager is still visibly unemployed.
steps.success_cue: The contained villager has changed into a librarian associated with the placed lectern.

steps.action: Face the librarian and right-click it to open the trading interface. Confirm that the interface identifies it as a novice librarian.
steps.success_cue: The novice librarian trading interface is open and its initial offer rows are visible.

steps.action: Inspect every currently displayed offer. For each offer whose output is an Enchanted Book, move the pointer over the output book and read its tooltip. The target roll is any offer whose enchantment name is Wind Burst, regardless of level or price. If the target roll is present, proceed to step 17. If it is absent, close the interface with Esc and proceed to step 14.
steps.success_cue: Either the target librarian roll has been identified, or the trade interface has been closed so the unwanted roll can be reset.

steps.action: Only when no Wind Burst offer was found and no trade has been completed, select a suitable tool or use Creative instant breaking and left-click the lectern to break it. Pick up or retain the lectern item for replacement.
steps.success_cue: The lectern block is absent and the untraded villager remains safely inside the pen.

steps.action: Wait for the villager to release the destroyed workstation and lose the librarian profession. Do not place the lectern again until the profession change is visible.
steps.success_cue: The villager has reverted from librarian to its unemployed appearance.

steps.action: Place the lectern again on the same floor space beside the villager, wait for the villager to become a librarian again, and return to step 12 to inspect the newly generated offers. Repeat steps 12 through 16 as many times as necessary, but stop breaking the lectern immediately when a Wind Burst offer is identified. Breaking and replacing a job block rerolls an untraded villager, while completing a trade locks its offers. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AVillager_trading_hall?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A new librarian roll is ready for inspection, or the reroll loop has ended because the target roll was identified.

steps.action: Once a Wind Burst offer has been identified, close the trading interface with Esc without breaking the lectern. Leave both the target librarian and its lectern in place for the remainder of the reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The target librarian remains beside its intact lectern, and no trade-reset action has been performed after identifying the target roll.

steps.action: Right-click the target librarian again. Select an offer other than the Wind Burst enchanted-book offer and note the exact item type and quantity shown in its input slot or slots. Close the trading interface with Esc.
steps.success_cue: The cost of one non-target offer has been recorded, and the target librarian has not yet been rerolled or traded with.

steps.action: Press E, search the Creative inventory for the exact input item or items required by the selected non-target offer, and move at least the displayed quantity into the player inventory. For example, obtain paper if the villager buys paper, or obtain emeralds and any second requested item if the villager sells an item.
steps.exact_input: Use the exact item names and quantities displayed by the selected non-Wind-Burst offer.
steps.success_cue: The player inventory contains every input item and quantity required to complete the chosen non-target trade once.

steps.action: Right-click the target librarian, select the chosen non-target offer, place the required items into the trade input slot or slots if they are not filled automatically, and click the output item once to complete the trade. Move the received item into the player inventory.
steps.success_cue: One trade has completed, the received item is in the player inventory, and the librarian's trade progress has advanced; its offers are now locked.

steps.action: With the same locked librarian, select the Wind Burst enchanted-book offer and note the exact item types and quantities required in its input slots. Close the interface, open the Creative inventory, and obtain at least those exact quantities. Use the displayed costs rather than assuming a fixed emerald price or enchantment level.
steps.success_cue: The player inventory contains the exact inputs required to complete the displayed Wind Burst book trade once.

steps.action: Right-click the locked librarian, select the Wind Burst enchanted-book offer, place the required items into the input slot or slots, and click the enchanted-book output once to complete the purchase. Move the purchased book into the player inventory.
steps.success_cue: The target transaction has completed once, and its enchanted-book output is in the player inventory while the librarian and lectern remain in place.

steps.action: Press E, search the Creative inventory for Mace and Anvil, and place one of each into the hotbar. Keep the purchased enchanted book in the player inventory.
steps.success_cue: The player has one mace, one anvil, and the book acquired in step 22 available in inventory.

steps.action: Select the Anvil in the hotbar and right-click a clear floor space near the pen to place it. Right-click the placed anvil to open its interface.
steps.success_cue: The anvil interface is open and both input slots are empty.

steps.action: Place the unenchanted mace in the anvil's left input slot and the purchased enchanted book in the right input slot. Click the mace in the output slot and move it into the player inventory. Do not perform any combat or additional Wind Burst testing before handoff.
steps.exact_input: Left input: Mace; Right input: the enchanted book purchased in step 22
steps.success_cue: The anvil transaction has completed, the output mace is in the player inventory, and the anvil input slots no longer contain the original mace and book.

stor.handoff_condition: A trade with the locked target librarian has been completed using the displayed Wind Burst enchanted-book offer, and the resulting book has just been combined with a mace at an anvil. The librarian and its lectern remain intact and no further interaction has been performed; begin observation from this state.
uncertainties: The report specifies no seed, coordinates, game mode, server requirement, villager biome, Wind Burst level, trade price, or expected number of lectern rerolls.

Offer generation is random, so the target may require many repetitions of the reroll loop. No command is used to force the offer because doing so would bypass the reported natural villager-trading condition.

The report does not state which experiments were enabled. The plan enables Update 1.21 because the relevant mace content belonged to that experimental feature set in this snapshot, and leaves Villager Trade Rebalance disabled to avoid adding an unrelated trade configuration.
Creative mode, cheats, fixed daytime, the containment pen, and the use of a non-target trade to lock the librarian are practical execution choices rather than explicit report requirements.

The report's phrase 'without limits' does not specify a restocking procedure or number of purchases. This plan performs one target purchase, which is sufficient for the supplied mace-application step and avoids unnecessary repetition.

source_meta._title: 'in_bounding_box' vertical position for 'spawn_particles' effect is anchored incorrectly

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 24w20a in a new singleplayer Creative-mode world with commands enabled. Load the report attachment bug.zip as a world data pack. Set particle display to All. Perform the test on an elevated transparent glass platform using a stationary, default-scale cow as the attacked mob. No particular world seed or coordinates are required by the report.
preconditions: Install and select the exact Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 24w20a in the Minecraft Launcher. Do not use the fix version 1.21 Pre-Release 2.
Obtain the report attachment named bug.zip. Keep the attached data pack unmodified and available to copy into the test world.
Use a vanilla client without mods that alter enchantments, entities, combat, particles, or rendering.
Use English UI labels for the paths below, or select the equivalent controls if the game language differs.
Ensure the observation or recording subsystem can begin inspecting the particle event immediately when the final attack is made, because the test requires only one trigger occurrence.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the Java Edition installation for snapshot 24w20a and start the game.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is open and the lower-left version text identifies the running game as 24w20a.

steps.action: From the main menu, open Options, then Video Settings. Locate the Particles setting and cycle it to All. Select Done until you return to the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The Particles video setting displays All, so particle visibility is not reduced by the client setting.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then Create New World. On the Game tab, set Game Mode to Creative and make sure Allow Commands is On. No specific seed is required.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Commands: On
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative mode and commands enabled.

steps.action: Before creating the world, open the More tab, select Data Packs, and select Open Pack Folder. Copy the unmodified bug.zip attachment into the folder that opens, then return to Minecraft. A data pack can be loaded from a .zip file placed in the world's datapacks location. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AInstalling_a_data_pack?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: bug.zip appears as an available data pack in the Data Packs screen.

steps.action: Enable bug.zip by selecting the arrow on its data-pack icon so that it moves to the Selected or enabled side of the screen. Select Done. If Minecraft asks for confirmation before enabling the pack, accept the prompt without modifying the pack.
steps.success_cue: bug.zip is shown in the enabled data-pack list and the world-creation screen can be resumed without a data-pack validation error.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait for world generation to finish. Do not continue while the loading screen is visible or while nearby terrain is still failing to render.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the new world, nearby chunks are rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Verify that the attached data pack is enabled. Press T to open in-game chat, type the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. Inspect the enabled-pack list in chat for an entry corresponding to bug.zip. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AInstalling_a_data_pack?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The command output lists the file data pack corresponding to bug.zip as enabled, and no data-pack loading error is displayed.

steps.action: Move to an open location. Double-tap Space to begin Creative flight, then hold Space to rise until the player's feet are at least about eight blocks above the terrain. Release Space and remain hovering.
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering in Creative flight with enough empty space below to build an elevated platform and view its underside.

steps.action: While hovering, press T, enter the following command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter. This creates a 9-by-9 glass floor one block below the player.
steps.success_cue: A square transparent glass platform is visible directly below the player, and chat reports that blocks were filled.

steps.action: Hold the Sneak/descend control, Left Shift by default, until the player is standing on the center area of the glass platform. Release the key after landing.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on top of the glass platform rather than hovering, and the transparent area beneath the platform remains visible.

steps.action: Obtain the required Diamond Sword. Press T, type the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. Because this is a newly created world with an otherwise empty inventory, the sword should enter the first available hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that one Diamond Sword was given, and a Diamond Sword icon is visible in the hotbar.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Diamond Sword. If it entered the leftmost hotbar slot, press 1; otherwise press the number corresponding to the slot where it appeared. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.success_cue: The Diamond Sword's hotbar slot has the selection outline and the sword is visible in the player's main hand.

steps.action: With the Diamond Sword still selected in the main hand, press T, enter the report's enchantment command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not replace or modernize the supplied enchantment identifier.
steps.success_cue: The enchant command succeeds, and the selected Diamond Sword has an enchanted visual glint or otherwise remains selected after a successful command message.

steps.action: Create a stationary target on the same platform. Stand near the platform center, press T, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter. The cow is placed two blocks away and NoAI prevents it from wandering off the platform; the report permits attacking any mob.
steps.success_cue: A living, stationary, default-scale cow is standing on the glass platform approximately two blocks from the player.

steps.action: Keep the enchanted Diamond Sword selected. Turn toward the cow and adjust position without jumping until the crosshair is aimed at the cow's body from normal melee range. Choose a viewing angle that keeps the cow's body, the glass at its feet, and some space beneath the glass in the camera view.
steps.exact_input: Mouse movement and normal movement controls; do not jump
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is on the cow, the cow is within sword reach, and both the upper body and transparent floor below it are visible.

steps.action: Stop moving and wait at least one second so the melee attack cooldown is fully charged. Confirm that no menu or chat screen is open and that the enchanted sword remains selected.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary, the gameplay view is unobstructed, and the next left-click will perform a fully charged sword attack on the cow.

steps.action: Attack the cow exactly once by pressing left-click while the crosshair remains on its body. Do not jump, repeatedly click, or make another attack before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The cow registers one melee hit and the enchantment's post-attack particle event has just been triggered.

stor.handoff_condition: The stationary cow on the elevated glass platform has just been hit exactly once with the selected Diamond Sword enchanted with bug:particle_post_damage. The camera still includes the cow's bounding area, the transparent floor at its feet, and the space beneath that floor; begin particle-position observation immediately.
uncertainties: The raw report names the required attachment as bug.zip but does not include its binary contents, directory structure, pack metadata, or enchantment JSON. The reproduction cannot proceed past data-pack loading unless the exact attachment is supplied and accepted by 24w20a.
The report specifies no world seed, coordinates, operating system, or server requirement. This plan therefore uses a new singleplayer world at an arbitrary open location.

The report says that any mob can be attacked and uses a scale-3 Husk only for its screenshot showcase, explicitly stating that default scale also reproduces the issue. This plan uses a default-scale stationary cow to avoid daylight burning, hostile movement, and unrelated particles.
The elevated glass platform, the cow's NoAI state, and the platform-building and summon commands are deterministic practical setup choices; they are not stated as mandatory conditions by the report.

The attached data pack was originally reported across multiple development versions. This plan follows the required first affected version, 24w20a; if bug.zip produces a version-format or registry-loading error in that exact snapshot, the attachment's compatibility cannot be resolved from the supplied report text alone.

source_meta.issue links: Cloners:outward:MC-271562:"projectile_spawned" Enchantment component triggers the enchantment effects BEFORE setting the projectile's default NBT
source_meta._title: "projectile_spawned" Enchantment Component runs predicates and effects on projectiles before all of their data has been assigned

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 in a vanilla single-player world. Use Creative mode with commands enabled so the test items and report-supplied enchantment can be applied deterministically. Install the provided projectile_spawned_bug_example_latest.zip datapack in the test world's datapacks directory.
preconditions: A Minecraft Java Edition installation using exactly version 1.21 is available. Do not use fix version 24w33a or any later version for this reproduction.
The report attachment projectile_spawned_bug_example_latest.zip has been downloaded and is accessible to the reproduction environment.
The Minecraft game directory and the test world's save directory are writable so the datapack can be installed.
Use the control bound to Use Item, which is right-click by default, when drawing and firing the bow.
Keep the in-game chat display available because the datapack communicates during each projectile-spawn event.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using an installation configured for version 1.21. Confirm the selected version before creating the test world.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is open and identifies the running game version as 1.21.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a new world named MC-273281-Repro. Set Game Mode to Creative and enable commands, then create the world.
steps.exact_input: World name: MC-273281-Repro; Game Mode: Creative; Allow Commands: On
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new Creative-mode world and can access the hotbar and chat.

steps.action: Wait before modifying the world files. Continue only after the terrain around the player has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, chunks are no longer visibly loading around the player, and player movement is responsive.

steps.action: Pause the game and return to the title screen so the world is closed before installing the datapack.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is displayed and the MC-273281-Repro world is no longer open.

steps.action: In the active Minecraft game directory, open the save folder for MC-273281-Repro and then open its datapacks subdirectory. Copy the provided zip attachment directly into that directory without extracting or renaming it.
steps.success_cue: projectile_spawned_bug_example_latest.zip is present directly inside the test world's datapacks directory.

steps.action: Return to Minecraft, open Singleplayer, select MC-273281-Repro, and enter the world again.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the test world, surrounding terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Reload the world's datapacks. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The reload completes without reporting that the provided datapack failed to load. The player remains in the world with controls responsive.

steps.action: Obtain one bow. Open chat with T, enter the command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A bow is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Obtain arrows for both test shots. Open chat with T, enter the command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A stack of arrows is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Make the bow the active item. If the bow is in the hotbar—the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen—use the mouse wheel or the corresponding number key to select its slot. If it is only in the main inventory, press E, move it to a hotbar slot, close the inventory, and select that slot.
steps.exact_input: Select the hotbar slot containing the bow
steps.success_cue: The bow is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Apply the report-supplied custom enchantment to the held bow. With the bow still selected, press T, enter the exact command from the report including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds rather than reporting an unknown enchantment or an inapplicable item, and the selected bow displays an enchanted glint.

steps.action: Move outdoors or to another location with a clear firing lane. Face approximately horizontally toward open space, with no block or entity immediately in front of the player. Keep the enchanted bow selected.
steps.exact_input: Use normal movement controls; aim with the mouse
steps.success_cue: The enchanted bow remains selected and there is enough open space in front of the crosshair for two arrows to be fired without an immediate point-blank collision.

steps.action: Fire the first arrow without fully charging the bow. Hold Use Item—right-click by default—for approximately 0.25 to 0.5 seconds, then release while the bow is still partway through its draw animation. Do not hold until the maximum-draw pose.
steps.exact_input: Hold right-click for approximately 0.25–0.5 seconds, then release
steps.success_cue: One arrow has been launched from a visibly partial bow draw, and the bow has returned to its resting position in the player's hand.

steps.action: Pause briefly between shots without changing items or closing the world. Wait until the first shot has completed its immediate processing and the player can begin drawing the bow again.
steps.success_cue: The enchanted bow is still selected, is no longer in its draw animation, and the Use Item control can start a new draw normally.

steps.action: Prepare the fully charged shot. Hold Use Item—right-click by default—and do not release until the bow reaches and remains at its maximum-draw pose. Holding for at least approximately 1.25 seconds avoids releasing before full charge.
steps.exact_input: Press and hold right-click for at least approximately 1.25 seconds; do not release yet
steps.success_cue: The bow is held at its maximum-draw pose and no longer appears to draw farther while right-click remains held.

steps.action: Release Use Item immediately after confirming that the bow is fully charged, thereby firing the second arrow. Do not perform another attack, command, reload, or item change after releasing.
steps.success_cue: The second arrow has just been launched from the fully drawn enchanted bow, after the earlier partially charged arrow.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has fired exactly two arrows from the bow enchanted with test:arrow_crit_detection: first from a partial draw and then from a confirmed full draw. The fully charged second arrow has just spawned, chat remains available, and no subsequent command, reload, item change, or additional shot has been performed. Begin observation immediately.
uncertainties: The report attachment's internal files were not supplied in the raw report, so the plan assumes projectile_spawned_bug_example_latest.zip is the updated datapack referenced by the report and is usable in final release 1.21.

The report does not specify single-player versus dedicated server, game mode, world seed, or location. A new single-player Creative world with commands enabled is used as the minimum deterministic setup and is not asserted to be a required bug condition.
The report describes partial and full charging qualitatively but supplies no exact timing. The timing guidance is an execution aid; the visible bow draw state is the controlling condition.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-301020:Piercing arrows do not pierce as expected at level IV when hit entities are on the same block
source_meta._title: Piercing arrows phase through mobs that are in the same block

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.5 in a new single-player Creative-mode world with commands enabled. Use an open, flat area with enough room to dig a 1×1 vertical pit and stand beside it. No world seed or coordinates are specified by the report.
preconditions: Launch exactly Java Edition 1.21.5, the first version listed as affected.
Use two adult mobs of the same type to guarantee equal hitbox dimensions; this plan uses two adult pigs.
Commands must be permitted because the deterministic setup directly summons both pigs at 1 health point, equivalent to half a heart.
Use a normal arrow as crossbow ammunition, not a firework rocket.
Do not damage, ignite, suffocate, or otherwise interact with the pigs after summoning them; each pig has only 1 health point.
Fire only one test shot, then immediately hand control to the observation subsystem.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select the Java Edition installation for version 1.21.5, and launch the game. Do not use the listed fix version or a newer installation for this reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen identifies the running version as Java Edition 1.21.5.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a new world. Set Game Mode to Creative and ensure commands are allowed. A Superflat world may be used to provide an unobstructed testing area; the report does not require a particular seed or terrain type.
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a Creative-mode world and can use commands.

steps.action: Wait before beginning construction. Do not continue until the nearby terrain has rendered and movement, block breaking, and chat commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are visible and the player can move and break blocks without loading pauses.

steps.action: Choose a solid ground block in the open area. In Creative mode, break that block with left-click, then break the block immediately beneath it. This creates a vertical pit that is exactly one block wide by one block long and two blocks deep, with a solid block still forming its floor.
steps.success_cue: A 1×1 opening extends two blocks below ground level and has solid walls and a solid floor.

steps.action: Drop or fly into the pit and stand on its bottom floor. Position the player wholly within the single bottom block so that relative summon coordinates place each pig in the same 1×1 space.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing at the bottom of the 1×1 pit.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the first summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The command creates an adult pig at 1 health point, disables its movement AI, prevents normal despawning, and tags it for verification.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and one stationary adult pig appears in the bottom block of the pit.

steps.action: Without leaving the pit, press T again and execute the second summon command exactly as written. Do not punch or otherwise damage the first pig.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and two stationary adult pigs are confined together within the same 1×1 bottom space.

steps.action: Verify the first pig's health. Open chat with T, enter the data command exactly as written, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports a Health value of 1.0f for the first tagged pig, corresponding to one health point or half a heart.

steps.action: Verify the second pig's health. Open chat with T, enter the data command exactly as written, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports a Health value of 1.0f for the second tagged pig.

steps.action: Exit the pit without touching the attack control. In Creative mode, double-tap Space to begin flying, then hold Space to ascend above the pigs and move onto an adjacent ground block. Do not break any pit wall or allow the pigs to leave the 1×1 space.
steps.success_cue: The player is outside the pit, while both pigs remain alive and together in its bottom 1×1 space.

steps.action: Obtain a crossbow. Press T, enter the give command exactly as written with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that one crossbow was given and the crossbow is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Place the crossbow in the hotbar and select it. If it was not placed there automatically, press E to open the inventory, left-click the crossbow, left-click an empty slot in the bottom nine-slot hotbar, and press E to close the inventory. Press the number key corresponding to that hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: The crossbow is visible in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Enchant the held crossbow with Piercing I. While the unenchanted crossbow remains selected, press T, enter the enchant command exactly as written, and press Enter. Piercing level I is sufficient for a shot intended to pass through two targets.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds; the selected crossbow has an enchantment glint and its tooltip lists Piercing I.

steps.action: Obtain one normal arrow. Press T, enter the give command exactly as written, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: At least one normal arrow is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: With the Piercing I crossbow selected, point away from the pigs to prevent an accidental test shot. Hold the Use Item control, right-click by default, until the loading animation and sounds finish. Release right-click only after the crossbow is fully loaded.
steps.exact_input: Hold right-click until loading completes, then release
steps.success_cue: The crossbow remains visibly cocked/loaded after right-click is released, and the held-item tooltip indicates that an arrow is loaded.

steps.action: Move to a ground block directly beside the pit. Look down into the opening and adjust position until there is an unobstructed line from the crosshair to the pigs; no rim or wall block should be between the loaded crossbow and their bodies.
steps.success_cue: Both pigs remain in the same bottom 1×1 space and the player's crosshair has a clear downward line of fire into that space.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the central body area where the two pigs overlap. Keep the Piercing I crossbow selected and do not use melee attack, break a block, or fire a preliminary shot.
steps.success_cue: The loaded crossbow is aimed through the shared space occupied by both pig hitboxes.

steps.action: Fire exactly once by pressing the Use Item control, right-click by default. Do not reload, fire again, or interact with either pig after this shot.
steps.success_cue: The crossbow discharges and the arrow reaches the shared 1×1 space containing the two pigs.

stor.handoff_condition: The Piercing I crossbow has just been fired once, and its arrow has reached the 1×1 space occupied by the two half-heart pigs. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem without firing another shot or interacting with the pigs.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, or whether the reproduction must occur in single-player or on a dedicated server. This plan uses a command-enabled Creative single-player world as the simplest deterministic setup.
The report permits any two mobs with the same hitbox size but does not identify a specific pair. Two adult pigs are used because identical entities necessarily have the same hitbox dimensions.
The report specifies a 1×1 hole but does not specify its depth. A two-block-deep pit is used to keep both pigs confined while allowing a clear downward shot.
The report does not specify the Piercing level. Piercing I is selected because only one additional target must be pierced; any level of Piercing supports a two-target shot.

The report says to get the mobs to half a heart but does not prescribe a damage method. This plan directly summons each pig with Health:1.0f to avoid accidental death or unequal health from manual attacks.
The report does not specify the exact shooting position or angle. This plan fires downward from the rim into the shared 1×1 space to avoid adding horizontal alignment or movement requirements.
The attachment videos were referenced in the raw report but their visual contents were not supplied, so no attachment-specific positioning or timing details were incorporated.
